comment: Frozen expectations about which corpus cases the attribution engine does NOT yet satisfy. This is the 'permanent memory' of known attribution defects: the set may only shrink, and a change in either direction must be made deliberately here and explained in the task report. 'wrongOwnerAtHighOrConfirmed' is the number that matters most - how many confident ownership claims are wrong. HISTORY. Task 03: 15 unresolved, 11 of 20 confident claims wrong. Task 04 (evidence kinds): wrong-owner HIGH/CONFIRMED 11 to 0, confident claims 20 to 4, unresolved still 15. Task 05 (path semantics): seven generic-token false positives refused outright; unresolved 15 to 3, desired met 9 to 21. Task 06 (ownership propagation and relationships): the ownership/relationship model exists, so the two NVIDIA cases are now blocked only by missing owner evidence rather than by a missing model; the generic relationship shape is proved by REL-SUBJECT-DATA-SYNTHETIC. Remaining: two NVIDIA cases that need Task 07 provenance to establish NVIDIA App ownership of the ancestor, and the Oxford publisher root, a provenance defect.
